questions.stem: Which of the following countries is likely to be affected less by earthquake?
explanation_steps: Earthquakes happen mostly along plate boundaries, where plates collide, separate or slide past each other.
Japan, Indonesia and Chile lie on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire'. Haiti lies on the boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates (it had a disastrous earthquake in 2010).
South Africa lies far inside the stable African plate, so it has only rare, weak tremors. Answer: C.
tips: Earthquake belts: circum-Pacific (Ring of Fire), the Alpine–Himalayan belt and the mid-ocean ridges. Stable old shields (southern Africa, Australia, Canada) have few earthquakes.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following countries lies on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire'?
explanation_steps: Peru lies on the western coast of South America, where the Nazca plate sinks beneath the South American plate.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: In the lowlands of Eritrea, schools are closed for summer vacation in May because of the effects of
explanation_steps: The Eritrean lowlands (the coastal plains and the western lowlands) are very hot, and the heat is worst from May onwards; temperatures often go above 40 °C.
So lowland schools begin their summer break earlier than highland schools because the climate is too harsh for classes. Answer: B.
tips: Highland schools close in late June and July when the kiremti rains fall; lowland schools close earlier because of the heat.

similar_questions.stem: The hottest part of Eritrea, where temperatures can rise above 45 °C, is the
explanation_steps: The Danakil depression on the southern coastal plain is one of the hottest places on earth.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.note: The textbook describes the lowland climate as hot; the link to the school calendar is general knowledge.

questions.stem: The type of natural vegetation known as Selva is commonly found in the ______ Climate.
explanation_steps: The textbook: the tropical wet (tropical rainforest) climate has dense, evergreen forests called Selvas (as in the Amazon basin).
Savanna climate has tall grass with scattered trees; Mediterranean climate has evergreen shrubs. Answer: A.
tips: Selva = the Amazon rainforest; the name comes from the Portuguese/Spanish word for forest.

similar_questions.stem: Tall grassland with scattered trees is the natural vegetation of the
explanation_steps: Savanna = tall grass with scattered drought-resistant trees such as acacia and baobab.
Answer: B.

explanation_steps: A ridge is a long, narrow stretch of high ground; a mountain ridge links several peaks along its crest.
A hill or mountain is one raised mass; a plateau is a high area with a flat top. Answer: C.
tips: On a contour map a ridge appears as long, narrow closed contours or V-shapes pointing downhill.

similar_questions.stem: An extensive area of high land with a fairly flat top and steep sides is a
explanation_steps: A plateau is a raised, flat-topped tableland.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following towns <u>is not</u> a zonal administrative center of Eritrea.
explanation_steps: Eritrea's six zones and their centres: Maekel – Asmara; Debub – Mendefera; Anseba – Keren; Gash-Barka – Barentu; Northern Red Sea – Massawa; Southern Red Sea – Assab.
Adi Keih is a sub-zone town in the Debub zone. Answer: C.
tips: Learn all six zone centres. Adi Keih, Dekemhare, Senafe and Segeneiti are towns in Debub, whose centre is Mendefera.

similar_questions.stem: The administrative centre of the Gash-Barka zone is
explanation_steps: Barentu is the zone centre of Gash-Barka.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Most of the major rivers in Eritrea flow
explanation_steps: The textbook groups Eritrea's rivers into the Red Sea (eastern), western and Danakil drainage systems. The largest rivers are in the western system: Anseba, Barka, Mereb (Gash) and Setit. 'Most of the rivers that drain into the Sudan start from the Central Plateau, Southern Plateau and Western Escarpment.'
They rise on the plateau and flow down the gentle western slope into the Sudan, that is westward. Answer: C.
tips: The eastern-escarpment rivers (Haddas, Alighede, Comayle) are short and steep; the long, large rivers flow west to Sudan.

similar_questions.stem: The river Haddas drains into the
explanation_steps: Textbook: the Haddas joins the Alighede to drain into the Gulf of Zula.
Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: The western-drainage rivers flow toward the Sudan: the Mereb-Gash and Setit flow west, but the Anseba and Barka flow north-west to north. Keyed C (westward); E (north-west) accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> the outcome of the internal forces of the Earth?
explanation_steps: Internal (tectonic) forces come from inside the earth and cause folding, faulting, earthquakes and volcanism.
Weathering is the breaking down of rocks at the surface by the weather, which is an external (gradational) process. Answer: D.
tips: Internal forces build up relief; external forces (weathering, erosion, deposition) wear it down.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is an external force that shapes the earth's surface?
explanation_steps: Erosion by rivers, wind, waves and ice is an external (gradational) process.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: An enclave country in the southern part of Africa is
explanation_steps: An enclave is a country completely surrounded by the territory of one other country.
Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa. Swaziland (Eswatini) is landlocked but borders both South Africa and Mozambique; Seychelles, Comoros and Mauritius are island states. Answer: C.
tips: The world's three enclave countries: Lesotho (inside South Africa), Vatican City and San Marino (both inside Italy).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following African countries is an island state?
explanation_steps: Madagascar is a large island in the Indian Ocean.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The branch of geography that studies the origin, site, shape and classification of towns and cities is called ______ geography.
explanation_steps: Urban geography studies towns and cities: their origin, site, situation, growth, shape (morphology), functions and classification.
Population geography studies the number, distribution and composition of people. Answer: B.
tips: Urban = towns and cities; rural = villages; settlement geography covers both.

similar_questions.stem: The branch of human geography that studies the distribution, density and growth of people is
explanation_steps: Population geography studies population size, distribution, density and change.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: All of the following are examples of cottage industries in Eritrea, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: Cottage (handicraft) industries are small, family-based units that use simple tools and local raw materials: pottery, weaving, basket making, leather work, jewellery.
A biscuit factory uses machines and hired workers and is a modern manufacturing industry. Answer: D.
tips: Cottage industry = at home, by hand, family labour. Factory = machines, many workers, mass production.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a modern manufacturing industry rather than a cottage industry?
explanation_steps: Cement production needs large machines and a factory.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The largest oil producing country in Africa is
explanation_steps: Nigeria has long been Africa's largest crude-oil producer (about 1.8–2 million barrels a day around 2020), mainly from the Niger Delta.
Libya and Angola are next; Gabon is a small producer and Uganda had not started producing yet. Answer: C.
tips: Africa's leading oil producers: Nigeria, Libya, Angola, Algeria, Egypt.

similar_questions.stem: Most of Nigeria's oil comes from the
explanation_steps: Nigeria's oil fields are in and off the Niger Delta.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin / U.S. EIA country data (crude oil production)
textbook_ref.note: Nigeria was Africa's top producer at the exam date (2020). In some months since 2021, output falls have put Libya or Angola briefly ahead.

questions.stem: ______ erosion involves the direct collision of raindrops with the ground causing soil particles to move.
explanation_steps: The textbook: splash erosion is caused by raindrops hitting bare soil and throwing soil particles into the air.
Sheet erosion removes a thin even layer; rills are small channels; gullies are deep channels. Answer: B.
tips: Water erosion sequence: splash → sheet → rill → gully (from the smallest to the most severe).

similar_questions.stem: The removal of a thin, uniform layer of topsoil by water flowing over a gentle slope is
explanation_steps: Sheet erosion removes soil evenly over a wide area.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Eritrea shares the <u>shortest</u> political boundary with
explanation_steps: Eritrea's land borders: Ethiopia (about 1,000 km), Sudan (about 680 km) and Djibouti (about 110–125 km).
Somalia and South Sudan do not border Eritrea. Answer: A.
tips: Eritrea has three land neighbours: Sudan (west and north), Ethiopia (south) and Djibouti (south-east).

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea shares its longest land boundary with
explanation_steps: The Eritrea–Ethiopia boundary (about 1,000 km) is the longest.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common characteristic of a region?
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the common characteristics of regions: every region has a location, an area (extent) and boundaries, and regions are arranged in a hierarchy (smaller regions inside larger ones).
All four options apply. Answer: E.
tips: Characteristics of a region: location, extent (area), boundary, hierarchical arrangement, homogeneity.

similar_questions.stem: A region defined by one or more uniform features such as climate or language is a
explanation_steps: Formal regions share a common characteristic throughout.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The center of the solar system is
explanation_steps: The textbook: the sun 'is the center of one of the solar systems of the universe'; the planets move around it.
The Sun is not listed, so the answer is 'None of the above'. Answer: E.
tips: Heliocentric = sun-centred (Copernicus). Mercury is the planet nearest the sun, not its centre.

similar_questions.stem: The largest planet in the solar system is
explanation_steps: Jupiter is the largest planet.
Answer: C.

explanation_steps: The textbook lists 'the Alps of Europe' with the Andes of South America and the Rockies of North America.
The Alps stretch across southern and central Europe (France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria). Answer: C.
tips: Young fold mountains: Alps (Europe), Himalayas (Asia), Andes (S. America), Rockies (N. America), Atlas (NW Africa).

similar_questions.stem: The Atlas Mountains are found in

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Ali Ghider is the largest cotton growing area' in Eritrea, near Tesseney in the Gash-Barka zone, irrigated from the Gash river.
Answer: A.

explanation_steps: Alighider lies near Tesseney on the Gash (Mereb) river.

questions.stem: A volcano which is inactive but not dead is called
explanation_steps: The textbook: a dormant volcano has not erupted for a long time but may erupt again; an extinct volcano is dead and not expected to erupt.
Answer: B.
tips: Active = erupts now or recently; dormant = 'sleeping'; extinct = dead.

similar_questions.stem: A volcano that is not expected to erupt ever again is
explanation_steps: Extinct volcanoes are dead.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The average number of years a person is expected to live at birth is called
explanation_steps: Life expectancy is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live if current death rates stay the same.
Answer: D.
tips: Life expectancy is an important indicator of development (it is part of the Human Development Index).

similar_questions.stem: The number of live births per 1,000 people in a year is the
explanation_steps: Crude birth rate = births per 1,000 population per year.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The fastest rate of urbanization in the world is found in
explanation_steps: Europe, North America and Australia are already highly urbanised (over 70–80% urban), so their urban share grows slowly.
Africa is the least urbanised continent but its towns grow fastest (about 3.5–4% a year), because of high natural increase and rural–urban migration. Answer: A.
tips: Rate of urbanisation (speed) differs from level of urbanisation (share): Africa has the lowest level but the fastest rate.

similar_questions.stem: Which continent has the highest percentage of its population living in towns?
explanation_steps: North America is about 80% urban.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.note: Africa has had the fastest urban growth rate since the 1990s and still does in 2026.

questions.stem: What type of slope is represented by evenly spaced contour lines on a map?
explanation_steps: The textbook: when contour lines are evenly spaced the slope is even (uniform).
Concave: contours close together at the top and wide apart at the bottom; convex: the opposite; cliff: contours merge. Answer: A.
tips: Close contours = steep; wide = gentle; equal spacing = even slope.

similar_questions.stem: Contour lines closely spaced near the top of a hill and widely spaced near its foot show a
explanation_steps: Steep at the top, gentle at the bottom = concave.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Elements of weather and climate consist of
explanation_steps: The textbook: the elements of weather and climate are temperature, air pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation (and cloud cover).
All four listed are elements. Answer: E.
tips: Elements (what we measure) differ from controls (what causes them: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea …).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a control (factor) of climate rather than an element?
explanation_steps: Altitude influences climate; it is not itself measured as weather.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The three branches of the East African Rift Valley converge at the
explanation_steps: The Red Sea rift, the Gulf of Aden rift and the main Ethiopian (East African) rift meet at the Afar triangle (Afar/Danakil plains), a triple junction.
Answer: A.
tips: Afar triple junction = Red Sea + Gulf of Aden + East African Rift. Part of it lies in the Southern Red Sea zone of Eritrea.

similar_questions.stem: The Danakil depression, part of the Afar triangle, lies mainly in

explanation_steps: The Danakil depression is shared by south-eastern Eritrea and north-eastern Ethiopia.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a cultural feature?
explanation_steps: The textbook separates natural (physical) features, such as rivers, hills and lakes, from cultural (man-made) features, such as villages, houses, roads, bridges and farms.
A river is natural. Answer: D.
tips: Cultural = man-made; natural = made by nature.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a cultural feature shown on a topographic map?
explanation_steps: A railway is built by people.
Answer: C.

explanation_steps: The Sahara (about 9 million km²) is the largest hot desert in the world. The Arabian desert (about 2.3 million km²) is second.
Answer: C. (Antarctica is larger if cold deserts are counted, but it is not an option.)
tips: Sahara = North Africa, from the Atlantic to the Red Sea.

similar_questions.stem: The Kalahari desert is found in
explanation_steps: The Kalahari covers Botswana and parts of Namibia and South Africa.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The planet in the solar system that has the smallest mean distance from the sun is
explanation_steps: Order of planets from the sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Mercury is the nearest (about 58 million km). Answer: A.
tips: Mnemonic: 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles'.

similar_questions.stem: The planet farthest from the sun is
explanation_steps: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a source for renewable energy?
explanation_steps: Renewable energy sources are replaced naturally: sun, wind, geothermal heat and flowing water.
Petroleum is a fossil fuel that took millions of years to form and runs out once used. Answer: C.
tips: Non-renewable: coal, petroleum, natural gas, uranium.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Coal is a fossil fuel.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The classification of the earth's atmosphere into four layers is based on the differences in
explanation_steps: The atmosphere is divided into troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere and thermosphere according to how temperature changes with height: it falls in the troposphere, rises in the stratosphere, falls again in the mesosphere and rises in the thermosphere.
Answer: D.
tips: Temperature decreases in the troposphere at about 6.5 °C per 1,000 m (the lapse rate).

similar_questions.stem: The layer of the atmosphere where almost all weather takes place is the
explanation_steps: Clouds, rain and storms form in the troposphere.
Answer: A.

questions.stem: The most important driving force for the development of a country is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Education is the major driving force for development.' Educated people use capital, resources and technology productively.
Answer: B.
tips: Human resource development (education and health) is the key to development in the textbook.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a social indicator of development?
explanation_steps: Literacy is a social (education) indicator.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is made of ice crystals formed near the ground when the temperature is below freezing point?
explanation_steps: When the air near the ground cools below 0 °C, water vapour turns directly into ice crystals on the ground and on plants; this is frost.
Dew forms the same way above freezing point as water droplets. Answer: B.
tips: Dew = water droplets (above 0 °C); frost = ice crystals (below 0 °C).

similar_questions.stem: Tiny water droplets that condense on grass on cool, clear nights above freezing point are
explanation_steps: Dew forms when the dew point is above 0 °C.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: In a soil profile, a layer that consists of partially weathered bedrock is called ______ Horizon.
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'C Horizon: A layer that consists of partially weathered bedrock. R Horizon: A layer that consists of hard bedrock.'
Answer: E.
tips: O–A–E–B–C–R from top to bottom.

similar_questions.stem: The soil horizon where materials washed down from above accumulate (illuviation) is
explanation_steps: The B horizon (subsoil) is the zone of accumulation.
Answer: D.

questions.stem: An equipment used to measure air pressure is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The instrument used to measure air pressure is called a Barometer.'
Anemometer = wind speed; hygrometer = humidity; thermometer = temperature; rain gauge = rainfall. Answer: B.
tips: Pressure is recorded in millibars; lines of equal pressure on a map are isobars.

similar_questions.stem: Lines on a map joining places of equal air pressure are called
explanation_steps: Isobars join places with the same pressure.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Deforestation in Eritrea has resulted in
explanation_steps: The textbook links Eritrea's deforestation to soil erosion, reduced rainfall and recurrent droughts, shortage of fuel wood and building material, and loss of wildlife habitats (many animals disappeared).
All four are results. Answer: E.
tips: Eritrea's forest cover fell from about 30% a century ago to under 1–2% today; afforestation and terracing are the remedies.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following helps to reverse the effects of deforestation in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Tree planting and terracing restore cover and control erosion.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a <u>river valley</u> civilization?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Historians call the civilization which emerged in the Indus River Valleys between 3000 and 1500 B.C.E, Harappan or Indus civilization', with its cities Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
The Greek, Incan, Mayan and Aztec civilizations did not grow up in a great river valley. Answer: C.
tips: The four early river valley civilizations: Mesopotamia (Tigris–Euphrates), Egypt (Nile), India (Indus – Harappan) and China (Huang He).

similar_questions.stem: The ancient Chinese civilization first developed along the
explanation_steps: Early Chinese civilization (Shang dynasty) developed in the Huang He valley.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Between 500 and 200 B.C.E., three major philosophies emerged in China. These three philosophies were Confucianism, Taoism and Legalism.'
Dualism (the idea of two opposed principles, such as good and evil in Zoroastrianism) is not one of them. Answer: B.
tips: Confucius = order, family and good government; Laozi = Taoism (harmony with nature); Legalism = strict laws and harsh punishment (Qin dynasty).

explanation_steps: Legalism held that people must be controlled by strict laws.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The language that <u>doesn't</u> belong to the Semitic linguistic group in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The textbook groups Eritrea's languages: 'Nilotic language group: Nara and Kunama; Cushitic language group: Hidareb, Bilen, Saho and Afar; Semitic language group: Tigrinya, Tigre, and the Rashaida (Arabic).'
Bilen is Cushitic (the Bilen descend from Agew groups). Answer: C.
tips: Semitic: Tigrinya, Tigre, Arabic (Rashaida). Cushitic: Bilen, Saho, Afar, Hidareb. Nilotic: Kunama, Nara.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following Eritrean languages belongs to the Nilotic group?
explanation_steps: Kunama and Nara are Nilotic languages.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>incorrect</u>?

options.A: History is a record of human past activities.
options.B: The term history is derived from a Greek word Historia.
options.C: History deals only with political aspects of societies.
options.D: Legends and myth constitute the largest part of History.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'History is a record of the past'; 'The term history is derived from a Greek word historia, meaning inquiry'. So A and B are correct.

History studies 'all human activities' (political, economic, social, cultural), not only politics, so C is incorrect. The textbook also says 'history is different from legends and myths', so D is incorrect.
Both C and D are incorrect. Answer: E.
tips: When two statements are wrong and a 'C and D' option exists, it is the answer.

similar_questions.stem: The Greek word 'historia', from which 'history' comes, means
explanation_steps: Historia means inquiry (investigation).
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which chronological order <u>is correct</u> about foreign conquest and colonialism in Eritrea?

options.A: Italy → Egypt → Britain → Ottoman Turkey → Ethiopia
options.B: Ottoman Turkey → Italy → Egypt → Britain → Ethiopia
options.C: Ottoman Turkey → Egypt → Italy → Britain → Ethiopia
options.D: Egypt → Britain → Ottoman Turkey → Italy → Ethiopia
options.E: Italy → Egypt → Ethiopia → Britain → Ottoman Turkey

explanation_steps: Ottoman Turks occupied Massawa and Hirghigo in 1557.
Egypt took over Massawa (1865) and Bogos/Keren (1872).
Italy began at Assab (1869/1882), took Massawa in 1885 and proclaimed the colony of Eritrea in 1890.
Britain ruled from 1941 (the British Military Administration) until 1952.
Ethiopia came in through the federation (1952) and the annexation (1962), until independence in 1991. Answer: C.
tips: Dates: 1557 Ottoman, 1865/1872 Egypt, 1890 Italy, 1941 Britain, 1952/1962 Ethiopia.

similar_questions.stem: The Ottoman Turks occupied Massawa and Hirghigo in
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'the Ottoman Turks occupied Massawa and Hirghigo in 1557.'
Answer: B.

Chaldiran (1514) was an Ottoman–Safavid battle; Macedonia is a region; Troy is a legendary city. Answer: C.
tips: Marathon (490 B.C.E.) and Salamis (480 B.C.E.) were the great Greek victories in the Persian Wars.

similar_questions.stem: The Persian king defeated by the Greeks at Marathon was
explanation_steps: Darius I sent the army that lost at Marathon.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>was not</u> among the reasons for the spread of Islam in Eritrea?

options.A: The advent of Prophet Muhammed's companions to Eritrea
options.B: Revival of trade in the Red Sea region

explanation_steps: The textbook: Eritrea was the first country in Africa to receive Islam when the Prophet's persecuted followers came (the first Hijra); 'with the rise of the Fatamids in Egypt and the consequent revival of trade in the Red Sea, the influence of Islam increased'; 'The Dahlak islands were the major gateway for the coming of Islam.'
The Agew migration brought Cushitic Agew groups (ancestors of the Bilen) from Wag and Lasta; it did not spread Islam. Answer: D.
tips: Channels of Islam into Eritrea: the companions (615 C.E.), Red Sea trade, the Dahlak sultanate.

similar_questions.stem: The major gateway for the coming of Islam to Eritrea was the
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'The Dahlak islands were the major gateway for the coming of Islam to our country.'
Answer: B.

explanation_steps: The textbook lists the five pillars of Islam: Shahadah (faith), Salaat (prayer five times a day), Zakat (giving a certain percentage of one's wealth to the poor), Sawm (fasting in Ramadan) and Hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca).
Answer: D.
tips: Five pillars: Shahadah, Salat, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj.

similar_questions.stem: The pilgrimage to Mecca that every able Muslim should make once in a lifetime is
explanation_steps: Hajj is the fifth pillar.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: Genghis Khan was the famous leader of the
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Led by their famous leader, Genghis Khan, Mongol armies spread…' across Asia; in 1258 the Mongols destroyed the Abbasid capital Baghdad.
Answer: B.
tips: Genghis Khan united the Mongols in 1206; his grandson Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty in China.

similar_questions.stem: The Mongol ruler who founded the Yuan dynasty in China was
